title: Scalar cup agrees with ordinary module cup
statement: For any scheme over a field, scalarCohomologyCup of two classes equals an ordinary module cup characterized by IsModuleCupProduct.

proof.text: Choose a computing CupResolutionPairing using the existing existence theorem.

The cycle-to-class maps of the two acyclic resolutions are surjective; lift the given scalar cohomology classes to cocycles. The local surjectivity proof expands the existing cycle projection, comparison homology isomorphism, and derived-object isomorphism.

Leibniz for the sectionwise pairing makes the paired section a target cocycle. Apply the supplied resolution characterization hypothesis, then use scalarCup_resolution_class_compatibility to identify the scalar cup with the target resolution class.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01F7 and 0FKV, compatible resolution-cup comparison; local Lean reduction through computing pairings and cocycle representatives

lean.statement:
theorem scalarCup_moduleCup_compatibility
    {k : Type w} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{w}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (F G : X.Modules) (p q : ℕ)
    (cup : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj F →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
      (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace q).obj G →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
      (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace (p + q)).obj
        (@id X.Modules (F ⊗ G)))
    (hcup :
      ∀ (D : CupResolutionPairing F G)
        (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val →
          cup (D.left.class p a) (D.right.class q b) = D.target.class (p + q) c)
    (a : scalarCohomology f F p) (b : scalarCohomology f G q) :
    scalarCohomologyCup f F G p q a b = cup a b
